title: Week of September 12, 2026
description:
BENDY: We cook one batch of honey sesame chicken on Thursday and it turns into Friday dinner with almost no work. Same chicken, cold, chopped, over crunchy stuff.

BUB: So Friday is just Thursday in a bowl.

BENDY: Friday is Thursday with a better attitude. But first, today. Saturday jobs, three of them.

BUB: Go.

BENDY: Pull the pork tenderloin and the chicken thighs out of the freezer and into the fridge. Tenderloin thaws overnight easy. Chicken needs a day and a half, so it goes in now for Monday's soup.

BUB: What about the Thursday chicken?

BENDY: Buy that fresh. Next job: mix the herb rub tonight and put it on the pork. Salt, garlic, smoked paprika, rosemary, black pepper, a spoon of brown sugar, olive oil to make it a paste. Rub it, wrap it, fridge. Overnight salt makes the inside taste seasoned, not just the crust.

BUB: And job three?

BENDY: Cauliflower. We need riced cauliflower twice this week, so do both heads today. Cut into chunks, pulse in the food processor till it looks like couscous, then stop. Store it in two bags.

BUB: Why stop?

BENDY: Two pulses too many and it's cauliflower mush. No fixing that. Also chop the kale for Wednesday and make the sesame sauce today if you've got ten minutes.

BUB: Okay. Sunday.

BENDY: Traeger Herb-Rubbed Pork Tenderloin with Roasted Brussels Sprouts & Apples. Traeger at 400. The tip: pull the pork at 145 in the thickest part and let it rest ten minutes. Go to 160 and it's dry and gray, and you can't undo that.

BUB: Ten whole minutes of waiting.

BENDY: That's when the sprouts finish. Halve them, cut-side down on the sheet pan, and add the apple chunks in the last twelve minutes so they don't turn to sauce.

BENDY: Monday, Creamy Chicken & Cauliflower Rice Soup, Slow Cooker. Low six hours, but the cauliflower rice goes in the last twenty minutes.

BUB: Or mush again?

BENDY: Or mush again. And stir the cream in off the heat, or it separates and looks curdled.

BENDY: Tuesday, Beef and Broccoli Stir-Fry with Zucchini Noodles. Slice the beef thin against the grain, and cook it in two batches.

BUB: Why two?

BENDY: A crowded pan steams instead of browning. Gray beef, no crust. And cook the zucchini noodles thirty seconds, tops. They're already almost done.

BENDY: Wednesday, Sausage, White Bean & Kale Soup. Brown the sausage first and leave the fat in the pot. Mushrooms go in after, straight into that fat, and they soak up all of it.

BUB: That's the good part.

BENDY: That's the whole soup. Kale in the last five minutes, still a little chewy.

BENDY: Thursday, Slow Cooker Honey Sesame Chicken with Cauliflower Rice. Set aside a cup and a half of chicken before we eat, or it disappears.

BUB: Learned that one already.

BENDY: Friday, Honey Sesame Chicken Chopped Salad, the leftover remix. Dress it right before it hits the table. Dress it early and the cabbage goes limp and watery.

BUB: And Saturday?

BENDY: Takeout. Nobody touches a pan.

BENDY: So: pork gets rubbed tonight, chicken goes in the fridge, cauliflower gets riced twice and no further.

BUB: And Thursday makes Friday.

BENDY: Thursday makes Friday. Hide that cup and a half.
